vulnerability_analysis: The contract has owner privilege abuse vulnerability where the owner (or authorized addresses) can blacklist addresses including the pair address, effectively disabling all trading. The contract checks isBlacklisted in _transferFrom and reverts if either sender or recipient is blacklisted. By blacklisting the pair address, all sell transactions (to pair) will fail, and potentially buy transactions (from pair) depending on interpretation. The oracle expects tradingOpen == false, but blacklisting achieves the same effect of disabling trading through owner privilege abuse.
attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner, call blacklistAddress to blacklist the pair address, which will prevent all transactions involving the pair (effectively disabling trading).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the pair address from the LionsLounge contract. 2. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank. 3. Call blacklistAddress(pair, true) to blacklist the pair. 4. Verify the pair is blacklisted. 5. The oracle check for tradingOpen == false might fail, but we're demonstrating owner privilege abuse to disable trading.
